**What I found**
The guard defends against a state the type system already rules out: `totalOf` is private, its parameter is the non-nullable `Order`, the module compiles under strict null checks, and both callers pass a literal they built lines earlier. There is no way to reach `throw new Error('missing order')` without breaking the type check first, so the check is dead on arrival — delete it and record *why* (the record calls this OBSOLETE, a necessity failure rather than a cost-vs-value trade).

**Why it matters**
Removing it drops three lines and one untestable branch, and takes with it a branch that will otherwise show up forever as uncovered in coverage reports or get "covered" by a test that casts through `any` to fake an impossible input. Leaving it costs little per day but teaches the next contributor that `Order`-typed parameters are untrustworthy, which is how this pattern spreads to the non-private functions where it is equally useless. Nothing beyond this function is affected: the error it throws has no caller-side handler in the code you showed.

Note the distinction, because it changes what a later audit may do: OBSOLETE holds unless an invariant changes. If `totalOf` is ever exported, or an `Order` starts arriving from `JSON.parse`, an `as Order` cast, or any other unchecked boundary, the argument reopens — and at that point the right guard is on `order.lines` being an array, not on `order` being null.

**Do this first**
1. Delete the `if (order === null || order === undefined) { throw ... }` block, leaving `return order.lines.reduce((sum, line) => sum + line.amount, 0);`, then run `tsc --noEmit` and the module's tests; if a test asserts the `'missing order'` throw, delete that test too — it can only pass by casting through `any`.
2. Later (trigger: the same guard appears in a second review): enable `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` for this package so the rule is machine-checked instead of caught by eye. It needs `strictNullChecks`, which you have.

**What I did not check**
I worked from your description of the module, not the source — I have no repo here. Confirm with `grep -rn "totalOf" src/` that the two callers are the only ones and neither passes a value that came from `JSON.parse`, an `any`, or an `as Order` cast, and `grep -rn "missing order" .` that nothing asserts on the message. I did not assess whether `order.lines` itself is guaranteed populated at every construction site; `grep -n "lines:" ` over those two callers settles it.

```text
Subject:        private totalOf(order: Order) null/undefined guard
Mode:           Retrospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: §1a impossible-state guard — null-guard on a non-nullable type.
                Trigger reachability fails: the function is module-private, the
                parameter is non-nullable under strict null checks, and both
                callers pass a locally constructed literal. Not §1c: the type
                annotation `order: Order` is already the canonical, machine-checked
                record of the invariant, so the guard documents nothing new.
Outcome evidence: not applicable
Decision:       OBSOLETE
Rationale:      The failure mode the guard prevents cannot occur in this stack, so
                worth scoring does not apply. Deleting it is structural, not
                budgetary: the case reopens only if the function is exported or an
                unvalidated `Order` enters from a boundary.
Next action:    Delete the guard block; drop any test that asserts the throw.
Verification:   Not run — no repository access. Closes with `tsc --noEmit`, the
                module's test command, `grep -rn "totalOf" src/`, and
                `grep -rn "missing order" .`
Minimal alt:    n/a — the guard has no reachable branch to preserve.
```
